entries.title: Word frequencies
entries.summary: Count literal words and report each count and its rate per 10,000 included word tokens. Words are normalized with NFC, case folding and straight apostrophes; the result keeps source digests and first-occurrence offsets for each word in each input.
inputs: A verified local CORE corpus, selected with --corpus DIRECTORY or corpus discovery.
Or an explicit regular UTF-8 text file.

settings.name: --provider / --input-file (alias --file)
settings.meaning: Use CORE or an explicit regular UTF-8 file; a file selects the file provider by default.

settings.name: --within / --passage
settings.meaning: Choose a CORE reader subtree or repeat exact passage UUIDs; otherwise use the whole source.

settings.name: --span START END
settings.meaning: Half-open offsets in original Unicode codepoints, in a file or exactly one --passage; do not combine with --within.

settings.name: --compare / --reference-*
settings.meaning: Optionally count an independent reference; --compare alone uses the whole target source. Reference provider, file or corpus, subtree, passages and span can be chosen separately.

settings.name: Tokenization (fixed)
settings.meaning: Unicode letters with combining marks and internal apostrophes; numbers and punctuation are not word tokens. No stemming or stop-word removal.

entries.output: sol.word-frequencies v1 JSON: CLI --json prints to stdout (redirect to save). ESSENCE Save writes words-<timestamp>[-N].sol-analysis.json under $XDG_DATA_HOME/sol/studies, or ~/.local/share/sol/studies.
limits: CORE includes eligible Hegel main-text paragraphs, quotations and list items under the three doctrine reader paths; pending source reviews and non-prose records are excluded, and trailing facsimile labels are masked. File input is verbatim and has no CORE eligibility filters.
Only wholly contained tokens count in a span; zero-token rates are null. JSON is limited to 16 MiB; input files to 64 MiB.
Rows sort by decreasing target count, then word; ESSENCE displays at most 2,000 rows and 1,000 occurrences for a selected word. Saved locations contain only the first occurrence per input.
Lexical counts do not measure concepts or similarity.

entries.title: Word comparison
entries.summary: Compare a target and a reference by their word rates, using each side’s own token denominator. Report target minus reference per 10,000 tokens and the log base two of target rate divided by reference rate; this is a descriptive comparison, without significance tests.
inputs: A word-frequency study with both target and reference.
Explicit current CORE or UTF-8 file sources for both sides when checking or exporting.

settings.name: --reference-* / --compare
settings.meaning: Set independent reference input and scope on sol analyze words; --compare alone uses the whole target source.

settings.name: --format csv|tsv
settings.meaning: Choose the words-export table format; default csv.

settings.name: Zero policy (fixed)
settings.meaning: No smoothing: a zero count makes the log ratio undefined; an empty denominator makes both measures undefined. Export leaves undefined numeric cells empty and supplies a status.

entries.output: The saved study is still sol.word-frequencies v1; comparison measures are derived. ESSENCE Export writes words-<timestamp>[-N].csv or .tsv beside studies; CLI words-export prints the verified table to stdout for redirection, including source bindings and the study SHA-256.
limits: CORE includes eligible Hegel main-text paragraphs, quotations and list items under the three doctrine reader paths; pending source reviews and non-prose records are excluded, and trailing facsimile labels are masked. File input is verbatim and has no CORE eligibility filters.
Overlapping scopes are permitted, including a passage compared with its whole book. Differences in edition, language or projection require care.
No p-values, confidence intervals or conceptual-similarity claims. Export recomputes against the selected sources and refuses changed bindings or counts.
The table retains study order, not order by effect size; an empty vocabulary produces a header only.
entries.cli: sol analyze words-export words.sol-analysis.json --input-file target.txt --reference-file reference.txt --format csv > comparison.csv

entries.title: Sentence lengths
entries.summary: Split text with deterministic punctuation rules and count word tokens in each sentence. Report mean, lower median, nearest-rank 10th and 90th percentiles, a length histogram, means by position within each input, and the twelve longest sentences.
inputs: A verified local CORE corpus, selected with --corpus DIRECTORY or corpus discovery.
Or an explicit regular UTF-8 text file; the entire file is one input, not separate paragraphs.

settings.name: --provider / --input-file (alias --file)
settings.meaning: Use CORE or an explicit regular UTF-8 file; a file selects the file provider by default.

settings.name: --within / --passage
settings.meaning: Choose a CORE reader subtree or repeat exact passage UUIDs; otherwise use the whole source.

settings.name: --span START END
settings.meaning: Half-open offsets in original Unicode codepoints, in a file or exactly one --passage; do not combine with --within.

settings.name: --reference FILE|-
settings.meaning: Optional CORE origin anchor, not a scope restriction; unavailable for file input.

settings.name: Segmentation (fixed)
settings.meaning: Punctuation . ! ? … with abbreviation, initial and bracket rules; a newline always ends a sentence. No language model or adjustable segmentation thresholds.

entries.output: sol.sentence-study JSON: CORE legacy calls produce v1, explicit providers/files/passages/spans produce v2, and ESSENCE saves v2. CLI --json prints to stdout; ESSENCE Save writes sentences-<timestamp>[-N].sol-analysis.json in $XDG_DATA_HOME/sol/studies (default ~/.local/share/sol/studies). Artifacts contain offsets and digests, not sentence text.
limits: CORE includes eligible Hegel main-text paragraphs, quotations and list items under the three doctrine reader paths; pending source reviews and non-prose records are excluded, and trailing facsimile labels are masked. File input is verbatim and has no CORE eligibility filters.
Punctuation rules target the English translation and can split or miss boundaries; lengths are not a model of Hegel’s syntax.
Spans keep only complete sentences, with cut sentences excluded. File position means describe the file’s retained sentences, not paragraph positions.
Legacy v1 JSON is limited to 1 MiB; provider v2 to 16 MiB; input files to 64 MiB.

entries.title: Exact term occurrences
entries.summary: Count one normalized lexical token across the corpus or one doctrine. Report total occurrences, rates per 10,000 tokens by doctrine, and representative passages with the first match in context.
inputs: A verified local CORE corpus, selected with --corpus DIRECTORY or corpus discovery.
One WORD that normalizes to exactly one word token.

settings.name: --doctrine being|essence|concept
settings.meaning: Restrict the count to one doctrine; default all three.

settings.name: --limit N
settings.meaning: Maximum representative passages, 1–100 (default 10); does not cap counted occurrences.

settings.name: --reference FILE|-
settings.meaning: Optional CORE origin anchor; does not restrict scope.

settings.name: --json
settings.meaning: Print the complete result rather than a human summary.

entries.output: sol.term-study v1 JSON on stdout with --json; redirect to a chosen file. Includes representative context text and source locations; this CLI does not automatically save a study.
limits: Eligible Hegel main prose only; pending reviews and non-prose are excluded and facsimile labels masked.
Exact normalized lexical matching only: no phrases, stemming, synonym matching or conceptual similarity.
Result JSON is limited to 1 MiB; representatives may be truncated even though totals cover the full scope.

entries.title: Prose-only input
entries.summary: Prepare eligible Hegel prose as a derived input for later analysis. Remove headings and images from the feature text while retaining canonical ancestry, headings and source references as metadata; no model is trained.
inputs: A verified local CORE corpus, selected with --corpus DIRECTORY or corpus discovery.

settings.name: --corpus DIRECTORY
settings.meaning: Select the complete canonical corpus; this command has no subtree or span setting.

settings.name: --json
settings.meaning: Export full prose text and metadata; otherwise print only a summary.

entries.output: sol.prose-input v1 JSON on stdout with --json; redirect to a private chosen file. passages[].text contains book text; no file is saved automatically.
limits: Requires a permanent corpus identity and a current verified generation.
Includes only Hegel main-text paragraphs, quotations and list items without generated-text or pending-review flags; empty projected text is excluded.
The projection is not canonical text and has no lexical normalization; headings are metadata, not features.

entries.title: Blind sentence-marking sample
entries.summary: Select the same explicit number of eligible whole passages from each doctrine using a reproducible seed. The private sample contains source text without the segmenter’s predicted boundaries, ready for human marking.
inputs: A verified local CORE corpus, selected with --corpus DIRECTORY or corpus discovery.

settings.name: --per-doctrine N
settings.meaning: Required number of passages per doctrine, from 1 to 1,000; each doctrine must have enough eligible passages.

settings.name: --seed N
settings.meaning: Required integer from 0 to 4,294,967,295; passage UUIDs and seed determine a SHA-256 ranking.

settings.name: --output FILE
settings.meaning: Required new private JSON path outside all Git checkouts; its parent must exist.

entries.output: Private review_version 1 JSON at --output, created owner-only without overwriting. Stdout is a receipt, optionally JSON with --json.
limits: Contains book text; maximum 8 MiB. Requires reader paths under /BEING, /ESSENCE and /CONCEPT.
Equal passage counts by doctrine form a stratified pilot, not a weighted book-wide error estimate.
A sample has no human marks and cannot yet be scored.

entries.title: Sentence-marking text form
entries.summary: Turn an original unmarked sample into a blind UTF-8 form for a text editor. The reviewer adds sentence breaks while preserving the original characters and spaces.
inputs: A verified local CORE corpus, selected with --corpus DIRECTORY or corpus discovery.
An original unmarked sample JSON, as FILE or piped stdin (-).

settings.name: --output FILE
settings.meaning: Required new private text path outside Git; its parent must exist.

entries.output: A private marking form at --output, owner-only and never overwritten; stdout is a receipt. The form contains book text and no predicted boundaries.
limits: The sample must still match the current corpus and be unmarked.
Reserved form delimiters in source passages are refused. The form is limited to 8 MiB.

entries.title: Import human sentence marks
entries.summary: Read added sentence breaks from a completed marking form against its original unmarked sample. Produce a new review JSON with declared human sentences or explicit passage exclusions, preserving the original sample.
inputs: A verified local CORE corpus, selected with --corpus DIRECTORY or corpus discovery.
The original sample JSON and its completed UTF-8 marking form.

settings.name: --reviewer NAME
settings.meaning: Required nonempty reviewer label; this declares authorship but does not certify human review.

settings.name: --output FILE
settings.meaning: Required new private review JSON outside Git; its parent must exist.

settings.name: FILE / FORM
settings.meaning: Either input can be - for piped stdin, but not both.

entries.output: Private review_version 1 JSON at --output, owner-only without overwriting; stdout is a receipt, optionally JSON.
limits: Original source text and form structure must be preserved; changed characters or spaces are refused.
Inputs must match the current corpus; private JSON and marking forms are limited to 8 MiB.
Import does not score or certify the marks.

entries.title: Sentence-boundary evaluation
entries.summary: Compare the unchanged punctuation segmenter with declared human sentence boundaries in a completed review. Report false splits, missed boundaries, precision, recall and F1 overall and by doctrine, with exact error offsets in JSON.
inputs: A verified local CORE corpus, selected with --corpus DIRECTORY or corpus discovery.
A completed private review JSON, as FILE or piped stdin (-).

settings.name: --json
settings.meaning: Print the full report with per-doctrine counts and error offsets instead of the summary.

entries.output: A boundary-evaluation report on stdout, JSON with --json; redirect to save. No study or review file is automatically written.
limits: Final passage ends are excluded from boundary scoring; explicitly excluded passages are not scored.
Undefined metrics are null when their denominator is zero. Scores measure declared marks, not proof of human review.
Requires current sample bindings and valid complete marks; equal per-doctrine sampling is not a weighted whole-book error rate. Review input is limited to 8 MiB.

entries.title: Verify a saved study
entries.summary: Recompute a saved term, word-frequency or sentence study against its current sources. Refuse invalid or stale results rather than treating their stored counts or paths as authority.
inputs: Saved sol.term-study v1, sol.word-frequencies v1 or sol.sentence-study v1/v2 JSON, as FILE or piped stdin (-).
The current CORE corpus or explicitly supplied original UTF-8 target and reference files.

settings.name: --corpus / --input-file / --reference-*
settings.meaning: Supply sources appropriate to the saved study; file paths are not recovered from artifacts. Saved provider scopes are reused unless explicitly overridden.

settings.name: --json
settings.meaning: Print a verification receipt; without it, print a verified study summary.

entries.output: Verification receipt or human summary on stdout; redirect if needed. Does not rewrite the artifact or automatically save a new study.
limits: Matching counts alone are insufficient: source bindings, digests and provenance must verify.
Verification establishes reproducibility against these inputs, not the quality of transcription, human review or interpretation.
Legacy term and sentence v1 artifacts are limited to 1 MiB; word and sentence v2 artifacts to 16 MiB.
